stories.title: Thousands still missing as Nepal-Tibet flood relief and recovery intensifies
stories.summary: Thousands of people remain missing after a catastrophic flash flood along the Nepal-Tibet border a week ago, as rescuers scramble to reach anyone who may be alive even as they turn to recovery. At least 1,114 people have died in Nepal and nearly 4,000 more are missing, according to Nepal's disaster agency. On the Tibetan side, the death toll stands at 16, and more than 500 people are unaccounted for, Chinese state media reports. The UN's humanitarian agency has said the response is entering a new phase, with authorities intensifying relief and recovery operations. In Nepal, efforts continue to rescue workers, potentially in the hundreds, believed to be trapped in hydroelectric station tunnels. A massive flash flood, believed to have been triggered by a glacial collapse, swept through a Himalayan valley last Wednesday, wiping out villages. Nearly 12,000 people have since been rescued, according to Nepal's disaster management agency. But thousands more, including hundreds of foreign nationals - from India, the UK, Australia, the US, Malaysia, and more - are still missing. A week on, fears are growing that the death toll will only rise. Chinese state media has not reported any survivors on the Tibetan side of the border, but the search continues. Beijing, which annexed Tibet in the 1950s, tightly controls the region. All information comes from state media and foreign journalists cannot travel there without permission.

stories.title: Moscow vows to respond as Germany announces shutdown of Russian consulate
stories.summary: Russian Ambassador to Germany Sergey Nechayev strongly rejected Berlin’s allegations of Moscow’s involvement in the incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport as unfounded and absurd
article_sentences: MOSCOW, September 2.

The German government has decided to shut down Russia’s consulate general in Bonn from September 18 over an early August drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said.
Russian Ambassador to Germany Sergey Nechayev strongly rejected Berlin’s allegations of Moscow’s involvement in the incident as unfounded and absurd.
TASS has gathered the key details of the situation so far.

Staff of the Russian consulate in Bonn and the Russian House in Berlin, along with their family members, are to leave Germany as part of measures taken by the country’s authorities following a drone incident at Leipzig/Halle Airport, the Russian embassy said in a comment.
According to the diplomatic mission, "the German authorities blamed Russia for preparing an act of sabotage without providing any evidence or arguments."

The embassy specified that Berlin had decided to shut down the Russian consulate in Bonn by September 18, 2026, and end the 2011 German-Russian intergovernmental agreement on cultural and information centers, effectively paving the way for the closure of the Russian House of Science and Culture in Berlin.
Russian Ambassador to Germany Sergey Nechayev strongly rejected Berlin’s accusations of Moscow's involvement in the drone incident as groundless and absurd.

He stressed that the hastily contrived act of provocation only served the interests of the Kiev regime, warmongers within the European political class and military industrialists interested in fomenting the Ukraine conflict.
Nechayev pointed out that the measures announced by Germany amounted to an unprecedented escalation of tensions that would not remain without consequences.

Germany’s new anti-Russian decisions, announced citing the drone incident at Leipzig Airport, are another "gross error" that harms the interests of the country’s own people, Russian President Vladimir Putin said.
In his view, the decisions result from Germany’s domestic political situation, particularly the difficulties facing Chancellor Friedrich Merz.

stories.summary: US forces launched fresh attacks on Iran Tuesday, including one that the Iranian Red Crescent said left four people dead at a wedding celebration, with Tehran vowing "severe punishment" for the strikes. France 24's correspondent in Tehran Reza Sayeh has the latest.

stories.title: ‘Tower of broken dreams’: French artist takes Eiffel Tower work to Burning man
stories.summary: A French artist from Saint-Malo-du-Bois in the Vendée region has taken a sculpture known as the “Broken Eiffel Tower” all the way to the United States. The 26-metric-ton structure was dismantled piece by piece to be shipped from the port of Le Havre before being reconstructed at the Burning Man festival in the Nevada desert. Caitlin Brown reports

stories.title: 450 applicants in a matter of seconds: The struggle to find rental flats in Paris
stories.summary: September is the time of year when students in France are scrambling for accommodation, and this year, the available units are scarcer than ever. A whole series of factors, including tougher regulation of ecologically non-compliant apartments, means there are even fewer on the market.

stories.title: Hollywood in retreat as Venice Film Festival kicks off
stories.summary: The Venice Film Festival kicks off on Wednesday with the glamorous cinema showcase handing George Clooney a lifetime achievement award on its opening night. But despite the American star’s presence, this year’s festival features a distinct lack of films from Hollywood, reports France 24’s film critic Emma Jones.
